title: Regional crisis text line: implementation study of a triage and queue protocol after two empty searches, data gate unknown
notes: Demanding level 3 path. The need names an implementation study and RE-AIM and no other design, so classifyFamily routes it to "implementation" at create; the problem reply repeats the typed constraints (G11). Two recorded fixture searches both return HTTP 200 with zero records (a narrow query, then the broader query the model proposed). Between them a well-behaved discovery reply returns no leads and no certainty (gradeOverall omitted, listed in omitKeys), so nothing can complete the stage: it stays incomplete and "not assessed" after the reply and after the second empty search (G1, G2). Only the investigator's on-screen confirmation completes Scan, recorded as scan.emptySearchConfirmation.by "investigator" (A3.2 section 1, D20); certainty stays "" through reload, reopen and export. A reopen after the Gaps stage checks that the confirmation and completion survive partial work. A hypothesis whose feasibility the model cannot judge carries null (stored null, "not assessed", never 50; G4). The decision cites no ledger claim (nothing was retrieved) and has one gate that stays unknown (the vendor data-sharing agreement is drafted but not signed), so acceptance is allowed and the action stays blocked to the export (G7; A2 item 9). No record ids are involved. Requires D20 (no certainty and no completion over empty searches, investigator confirmation, "not assessed"), S11 (selectionStatus, actionStatus, basis) and D5 (status text). Catches: completion or certainty from an empty search or a model reply, a confirmation that a model could write, an unknown gate treated as met, a null score shown as a number, and state lost on reopen.

inputs.need:
I am a psychiatrist and the clinical lead for our region's crisis text line, which is run by a community mental health agency together with our hospital's psychiatry department. People in distress text a short number and are answered by trained volunteer responders, with two paid counsellors on shift for escalation. Over the last year the median time to the first human reply has risen from about 3 minutes to 11 minutes in the evenings, and about 1 in 8 conversations are abandoned before anyone answers. Texters who wait tell us they feel ignored at the worst moment.

The agency has agreed a new triage and queue protocol: an automated first reply within 30 seconds, keyword flagging of high-risk messages (for example mentions of a plan or means) so they jump the queue, and a surge roster of on-call counsellors who log in when the queue passes 10 texters. The protocol goes live across all shifts in January.

I want to evaluate this as an implementation study rather than a comparison of two groups, because the protocol will go live for everyone at once. We need to know whether it is delivered as intended (how often flagged messages are answered first, how often the surge roster logs in on time), whether volunteers accept it, and whether time to first human reply and abandoned conversations improve. I am thinking of RE-AIM as the frame. Our data come from the text platform's logs, which are held by the platform vendor, and the agency has not yet signed a data-sharing agreement that would give us message-level timestamps. We have no funding beyond staff time, and we must not read message content beyond the keyword flag.
inputs.constraints: No funding beyond staff time. Evaluators may not read message content; only timestamps, queue data and the keyword flag may be used. The protocol goes live for all shifts in January 2027, so there is no concurrent comparison group. Research activities may take no more than 20 minutes of each volunteer's time.
localFacts: The agency board approved the triage and queue protocol for all shifts from 11 January 2027 (board resolution CTL-2026-09).
Message-level timestamps are held by the platform vendor; the data-sharing agreement between the agency and the vendor is drafted but not signed.
In the 12 months to August 2026 the line handled about 14,800 conversations; the evening median time to first human reply rose from about 3 to 11 minutes.
The hospital research ethics board approved the evaluation on 2026-09-09 (REB-PSY-2026-071), conditional on a signed data-sharing agreement with the vendor.

response.title: Crisis text line triage and queue protocol: delivery, acceptance and time to first human reply
response.subtitle: Implementation study with RE-AIM outcomes and an interrupted time series of service measures
response.statement: Evening waits for a first human reply on the regional crisis text line have risen to a median of about 11 minutes and about 1 in 8 conversations end before anyone answers. A triage and queue protocol (automated first reply, keyword flagging of high-risk messages, surge roster) goes live for all shifts in January 2027. The evaluation will establish whether the protocol is delivered as intended, accepted by volunteers, and followed by shorter waits and fewer abandoned conversations.
response.whoAffected: People in crisis who text the line, many of them young or unable to speak safely by phone; volunteer responders and paid counsellors; the agency and the hospital psychiatry department.
response.whatHurts: A long wait at the moment of crisis can deepen distress or end contact; texters describe feeling ignored. Volunteers carry the pressure of a queue they cannot clear.
response.currentPractice: First-come first-served queue, no automated acknowledgement, two counsellors per shift for escalation, and no systematic monitoring of waits beyond monthly platform summaries.
response.whyNow: The protocol goes live on 11 January 2027, the ethics board has approved the evaluation on condition of a data-sharing agreement, and pre-implementation data exist only in the vendor's logs.
response.constraints: No funding beyond staff time. Evaluators may not read message content; only timestamps, queue data and the keyword flag may be used. The protocol goes live for all shifts in January 2027, so there is no concurrent comparison group. Research activities may take no more than 20 minutes of each volunteer's time.
response.patientCenteredGoal: Everyone who texts the line in crisis receives a human reply quickly, with the most urgent messages answered first, without anyone reading more of their words than their care requires.
response.summary: Problem framed as an implementation question about a service-wide protocol, with delivery, acceptance and service outcomes.

response.reading: Waiting sits between demand in the evening and a first-come queue that treats every texter alike. The protocol changes three things at once: acknowledgement, order and capacity. Whether it works depends on the keyword flag catching risk, on counsellors logging in when the surge roster calls, and on volunteers trusting the new order. Both recorded searches were empty, so every node below comes from the investigator's account and local facts, not from retrieved evidence.

response.rationale: The protocol goes live for every shift at once, so the evaluation is an implementation study: RE-AIM organises reach, adoption, implementation fidelity and maintenance, and an interrupted time series of weekly service measures, with season and demand as covariates, estimates the change in waits. Both recorded searches were empty, so the design rests on the investigator's local facts and approvals rather than on retrieved evidence. Reporting follows StaRI.
alternatives: Stepped introduction of the protocol by shift with a comparison (refused: the board has approved go-live for all shifts at once)
Simple before-after comparison of two months (refused: cannot separate the protocol from season and demand)
Satisfaction questionnaire for texters (refused: contacting anonymous texters adds burden at a moment of crisis)
response.whyNotMoreComplex: A controlled design is ruled out by a service-wide go-live; an interrupted time series with fidelity measures is the strongest design the situation allows and uses data the line already produces.

decision.statement: Evaluate the triage and queue protocol from its go-live on 11 January 2027 as an implementation study, with RE-AIM delivery and acceptance outcomes and an interrupted time series of evening time to first human reply and abandoned conversations, starting the analysis only when message-level timestamps are available under a signed data-sharing agreement.

response.overview: Implementation study of a service-wide triage and queue protocol on a regional crisis text line, using platform logs for an interrupted time series (52 weeks before and 26 weeks after go-live) and RE-AIM delivery and acceptance measures.
response.population: All conversations opened on the line from 12 January 2026 to 11 July 2027; evening shifts (18:00 to 24:00) for the primary outcome; all volunteer responders active after go-live for acceptance measures.
response.exposure: The protocol from 11 January 2027: automated acknowledgement within 30 seconds, keyword flag moving high-risk messages to the front of the queue, and a surge roster triggered when more than 10 texters are waiting.
response.procedures: Once the agreement is signed, the vendor exports de-identified conversation records (open time, first automated reply, first human reply, close or abandonment time, flag time, queue length, counsellor log-in times) without message text. The agency's data lead builds weekly series. Volunteers complete a four-item acceptability scale at weeks 8 and 24 (under 5 minutes each). Fidelity is computed from queue order and log-in times.

response.theoreticalFramework: RE-AIM for reach, adoption, implementation and maintenance; no additional determinant framework until fidelity data show where delivery fails.
response.summary: Interrupted time series with one primary outcome, one secondary, two fidelity measures and one balancing measure, gated on the vendor agreement.

response.designSummary: Interrupted time series of weekly evening medians with segmented regression, plus descriptive fidelity and acceptance measures.
response.sampleSize: The line handles about 285 conversations a week, about 110 of them in evening shifts, so each weekly median is estimated from roughly 110 conversations. With 52 pre-implementation and 26 post-implementation weeks, a weekly standard deviation of about 2 minutes around the trend and lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.3, segmented regression has about 80 percent power to detect an immediate level change of 2.5 minutes at two-sided alpha 0.05; the hoped-for fall from 11 to 5 minutes is well above this. The number of weeks is fixed by the go-live date and the 26-week reporting window.
response.primaryAnalysis: Segmented regression of the weekly evening median time to first human reply with terms for pre-implementation trend, level change and slope change at go-live, adjusted for weekly demand and a holiday indicator, with Newey-West standard errors for autocorrelation.
response.secondaryAnalysis: Same model for the weekly proportion of abandoned conversations (binomial); fidelity proportions with 95 percent intervals by month; acceptability scores at weeks 8 and 24; counsellor overtime described.
response.missingData: Weeks with platform outages are flagged and excluded from the model with a sensitivity analysis that includes them; missing volunteer questionnaires are reported, not imputed.
response.multiplicity: One primary outcome; the other measures are descriptive or secondary and reported with intervals.
response.software: R; analysis code and outcome definitions archived before the vendor export is received.
overfittingGuards: Model terms fixed before the export
No searching for alternative change points
Covariates limited to demand and holidays
Analysis starts only after the data gate is met
response.summary: Seventy-eight weekly points give about 80 percent power for a 2.5-minute level change; fidelity and acceptance are descriptive.

response.risks: The evaluation adds no contact with texters. Risks are re-identification from timestamps, and pressure on volunteers if fidelity data are used to judge individuals; data are aggregated by week and never reported by responder.
response.consent: A waiver of consent for de-identified conversation records, granted by the ethics board on condition of the data-sharing agreement; volunteers give verbal consent for the acceptability scale and may skip it.
response.data: The vendor exports timestamps, queue and flag fields without message text; the agency holds the only key to shift rosters; the analysis file is kept on the hospital research server with access limited to two analysts.
response.equity: PROGRESS-Plus: texters who are young, rural, LGBTQ+ or writing in a language other than English may be served differently; the keyword list is English only, so flag rates and waits are reported by conversation language and time of day, and the agency is asked to review the list with community partners.
response.effectiveness: Success is a sustained fall in evening waits and abandonment with the flag and surge roster delivered as designed; a failure of delivery points to a fix rather than abandoning the protocol.
response.efficiency: Uses data the platform already records; staff time only.
response.costs: Analyst and clinical lead time within existing roles; any vendor fee for the export is not yet known.
response.grants: None needed for the evaluation; results could support a regional mental health services grant for sustaining the surge roster.
response.partnerships: The agency's data lead and volunteer coordinator, two volunteer responders, a youth advisory group member with lived knowledge of crisis services, and the vendor for the export only.
response.rebPath: Approved by the hospital research ethics board on 2026-09-09 (REB-PSY-2026-071), conditional on a signed data-sharing agreement; no analysis begins before the agreement is signed.
response.limitations: No concurrent comparison; the keyword flag's accuracy is not measured against clinical judgement; message content is not examined.
response.summary: No texter contact, a consent waiver conditional on the data agreement, and equity reporting by language and time of day.

ethics.rebPath.includes: conditional on a signed data-sharing agreement

response.partnershipPlan: Two volunteer responders and a member of the agency's youth advisory group review the outcome definitions and the acceptability scale; the volunteer coordinator shares monthly fidelity summaries at team meetings.
response.socialListening: A three-month read of public posts that mention the line by name, recorded as composites without usernames and without replying.

response.title: Implementing a triage and queue protocol on a regional crisis text line: an interrupted time series and RE-AIM evaluation
response.abstract: Objective: to evaluate delivery, acceptance and service outcomes of a triage and queue protocol introduced on all shifts of a regional crisis text line in January 2027. Design: implementation study with an interrupted time series of weekly evening time to first human reply (52 weeks before, 26 after) and RE-AIM fidelity and acceptance measures. Results will be written after the vendor export.
response.introduction: Waits on crisis text lines occur at the moment of greatest need. Two recorded searches found no evaluation of queue protocols for text-based crisis services, so this evaluation relies on the line's own data.
response.methods: De-identified platform records without message text are analysed with segmented regression adjusted for demand and holidays; fidelity is computed from queue order and log-in times; volunteers rate acceptability at weeks 8 and 24. Analysis starts only after the data-sharing agreement is signed.
response.results: No data have been received yet. The report will present the time series, fidelity proportions, acceptability and counsellor overtime.
response.discussion: The discussion will interpret the change in waits against demand and season and explain any shortfall in delivery.
response.limitations: No concurrent comparison; English-only keyword flag; no measure of clinical outcomes after the conversation.
response.conclusion: To be written after analysis; limited to delivery and service outcomes on this line.
response.summary: StaRI-structured draft; the analysis waits on the data gate.
